prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and bioactive form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B010 first, but unanimity is not the argument. The argument is that the chain from physiology to therapy is unusually complete and independently confirmed: Holst's human physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action, Mojsov's identification of the bioactive truncated peptide, and Drucker's receptor biology and demonstration that the peptide could be exploited therapeutically. The resulting drugs are supported by large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. A single-achievement prize with these three names rewards discovery, not only development, and the scale of benefit to humankind is hard to match elsewhere on the shortlist. Timing is not a concern.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener's group is disputed, Habener is not among the credited names, and Knudsen's medicinal chemistry (acylated, long-acting analogues) is what made the drugs work. A three-person cap forces us to choose between rewarding hormone discovery and rewarding drug design, and either choice leaves a credible contributor out. I am also aware that a prize built on a contested allocation may age worse than one for a cleaner pairing such as B020.

responses.point: The chair treats Holst, Drucker and Mojsov as the strongest basic-science trio and sees Knudsen's liraglutide/semaglutide work as mainly industrial drug development, leaving her out.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and have kept it, but I would not call Knudsen's contribution merely industrial. Making a peptide with a half-life of days instead of minutes is a scientific problem, and it is what turned the physiology into a therapy. I would hold that against the citation, so I have worded it around the bioactive peptide and the physiology that enabled therapy, and not around the drugs themselves. If the committee wants the prize to name the drugs, Knudsen has to be reconsidered, and that would cost us Mojsov or Drucker.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius proposes a two-person CAR-T configuration (June, Sadelain) without Rosenberg, on the grounds that Rosenberg's decisive contribution lies in broader adoptive T-cell therapy and Eshhar's original concept is uncredited.
responses.response: I share the concern about Rosenberg: his claim is adoptive cell transfer, not CAR design, and on this ballot the origin of the CAR concept sits with Eshhar, who is not credited. That is why I keep B006 only as an alternative. A June-Sadelain pair is cleaner scientifically but leaves the conceptual origin unrecognized, which is a weaker position than B010 faces, where the whole chain of discovery is represented even if one name is contested.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B010 first but flags that whether Mojsov or an industrial developer belongs in the trio is contested, and that he has not verified the priority details.
responses.response: I am in the same position on priority: I rely on recall and cannot settle Mojsov versus Habener from the supplied material. The practical difference is that Mojsov's work identified the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, which is the step the incretin physiology and later pharmacology depended on, so her inclusion is better supported than adding an industrial name. I would want the committee to test this against the primary papers before the final ballot instead of assuming it.

responses.point: Linnarsson puts B045 (SMN2 antisense) third and B049 (organoids) sixth, while ranking B010 and B008 first and second.
responses.response: I do not share the enthusiasm for B008 as a runner-up. Six credited names with a discovery/deployment split and disputed priority between Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Boyden and Deisseroth means any trio is open to challenge, and it is chiefly a research tool. B045 is a stronger mechanism-to-drug story, but it is younger and depends on Krainer and Bennett alone being the right pair. I would keep B006 and B020 ahead of both if B010 failed.

uncertainties: Whether Habener's group should be credited and whether that displaces Mojsov or Drucker in the final trio.
Whether the citation should emphasize physiology and peptide biology or the therapeutic development, which decides whether Knudsen belongs.
I rely on recall for priority details and have not verified them against the primary literature.
If B010 does not secure a majority, the fallback is unclear because B006 has no first-place support and an incomplete attribution.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share an institution (Karolinska Institutet) with colleagues, but none of the shortlisted candidates is connected to my work or collaborators, so I see no need for recusal.
